en: The Scripture of the Six-Syllable Divine Mantra King;
Omitted from the Kaiyuan Catalogue, translated by an unknown person, appended to the Liang Records.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying in the Jeta Grove in the kingdom of Śrāvastī. At that time...
There was a non-Buddhist Caṇḍāla woman who specialized in committing various evils,
such as practicing sorcery with talismans and incantations,
or serving mountain deities, tree spirits, and the spirits dwelling beneath trees.
The sun, moon, five planets, Southern Dipper, and Northern Pole Star—
all *piśācas*, miscellaneous māras, and malevolent spirits—
seek to bewitch and delude the Venerable Ānanda and all virtuous people.
There were as many such [beings] as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.
At that moment, the Tathāgata, seeing that Ānanda was dazed and out of sorts,
and out of compassion for all sentient beings of the three periods of time, [acted accordingly].
I shall now expound for you this King of Six-Syllable Divine Mantra Sūtras,
which was spoken by previous Buddhas and is now spoken by me as well.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:

Andharī | Padarī | Karoṭicayūre | Tiṣyavati | Binduvati | Dhatūre | Dhakure | Dhakumati | Sumati | Andhārandhara | Dandāradidura | Dhanayaṇḍa | Manda-vati | Anānaya | Madhumavati | Karada-cayurā-bhaṇḍagamī | Tiyaṃvati | Bindumati | Aravagati | Vitha-vitiṇi | Cittha-vitiṇi | Cittha-vitiṇi | Svāhā. If anyone should cast an evil spell or curse against such-and-such a person...
Whether it has been done, or is yet to be done—
whether by a deva, a māra, a nāga,
a yakṣa, or a rākṣasa.
Whether they be hungry ghosts (preta),
kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, piśācas, ābhāsvaras, or upabhāsvaras.
Whether they be Jīvakas, Kharoṣṭhas, Vedas, or Upavedas;
whether they be śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas.
Whether they be Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, or Śūdras;
whether they be Mātaṅgas or Mātaṅga women, Caṇḍālas or Caṇḍāla women,
or slaves or slave girls.
Whether they be men or women,
or non-Buddhist Nirgranthas, or male and female non-Buddhist renunciants—
such various kinds of people, if they should employ curses, incantations, or sorcery;
I now [rely] upon this Six-Syllable Divine Mantra King Sūtra;
if one acts as a celestial being in the heavens, it shall be extinguished there in the heavens;
if one acts as a human being on earth, it shall be extinguished there on earth.
If one acts upward, one extinguishes it by acting upward;
if one acts downward, one extinguishes it by acting downward;
if one acts upon a wall, one extinguishes it by acting upon the wall.
If one acts while attached to a wall, one perishes while attached to a wall.
If one acts within the Milky Way, one perishes within the Milky Way.
If one acts within empty space, one perishes within empty space.
If it is performed upon the earth, it is extinguished upon the earth;
if it is performed beneath the earth, it is extinguished beneath the earth;
if it is performed beyond the eight directions, it is extinguished beyond the eight directions.
If it arises within the six directions, it ceases within the six directions.
If it arises amidst the drifting winds, it ceases amidst the drifting winds.
If it arises at the edge of the great waters of the four seas, it ceases at the edge of the great waters of the four seas.

If one creates [the perception of] rivers, the Yangtze, the Huai, or the Ji within the midst or at the edge of rivers, the Yangtze, the Huai, or the Ji, they will cease right there within the midst or at the edge of those rivers, the Yangtze, the Huai, or the Ji.

If one creates [the perception of] embankments or ponds within the midst or at the edge of embankments or ponds, they will cease right there within the midst or at the edge of those embankments or ponds.
If one performs it at the edge of water, it is extinguished at the edge of water.
If one performs it among mountains, rivers, valleys, mounds, or pits, it is extinguished among mountains, rivers, valleys, mounds, or pits.
If they arise within the boundaries of the five sacred mountains, they cease within the boundaries of the five sacred mountains;
if they arise within the boundaries of great marshes, forests, or thickets, they cease within the boundaries of great marshes, forests, or thickets.
If they arise within the interior or exterior of a large or small tree or blade of grass, they cease within the interior or exterior of that same large or small tree or blade of grass.
If they arise within the roots, stems, or other parts of a plant, they cease within the roots, stems, or other parts of that same plant.
If it is within the center or edge of a large or small path, one should eliminate it by making it within the center or edge of a large or small path.

If it is within the center or edge of a large or small crossroads, one should eliminate it by making it within the center or edge of a large or small crossroads. If it is within the center or edge of the outer gate of a castle, town, village, or hamlet, one should eliminate it by making it within the center or edge of the outer gate of a castle, town, village, or hamlet.
If it is committed within a castle, village, or town, it is extinguished within that castle, village, or town.
If it is committed outside the palace or by the inner gate, it is extinguished outside the palace or by the inner gate.
If it arises within the palace gates, it shall be extinguished within the palace gates;
if it arises at the edge of a cemetery, it shall be extinguished at the edge of the cemetery;
if it arises within the walls or boundaries of a house or residence, it shall be entirely extinguished therein.
If it was made on the roof-ridge, one should extinguish it on the roof-ridge;
if it was made at the edge of a pillar, one should extinguish it at the edge of a pillar;
if it was made below the base of a pillar, one should extinguish it below the base of a pillar.
If it arises within excrement or soil, it ceases within excrement or soil.
If it arises within a well, a hearth, a mortar, or a millstone, it ceases within a well, a hearth, a mortar, or a millstone.
If it is made upon the edge of a hearth, extinguish it upon the edge of the hearth.
If it is made upon the edge of a latrine, extinguish it upon the edge of the latrine.
If it is made upon the edge of a vehicle or its equipment, extinguish it upon the edge of the vehicle or its equipment.
If one makes additions or subtractions to the saddle, horse trappings, or their various components, one must eliminate those additions or subtractions.
If one makes additions or subtractions to beds, mats, clothing, blankets, rugs, boots, hats, or miscellaneous utensils, one must eliminate those additions or subtractions.
If one eliminates [the obstacles] at the very edge of all food and drink, or if those who are nearby perform such acts,
or wherever one is walking, standing, sitting, or lying down— in all such cases, they are entirely eliminated.
If one acts during the day, one eliminates it during the day;
if one acts at night, one eliminates it at night;
if one acts constantly throughout both day and night, one eliminates it throughout both day and night.
This mantra can sever the paths of the mantras of Śakra;
it can sever the paths of the mantras of Brahmā;
it can sever the paths of the mantras of the Four Heavenly Kings.
Furthermore, it can completely sever all malevolent spirits, demonic incantations, and worldly arts and techniques.
If anyone performs evil curses, bewitching spells, or imprecations against a certain person,
as well as the administration of poisons, this shall utterly extinguish them all.
Whether caused by khaṇḍa, vetāla, yakṣa, or pūtana,
all such afflictions shall be utterly extinguished; all evils shall be completely eliminated,
and they shall be replaced by manifold virtues.
May this mantra be ever auspicious.
By means of these words of truth,
may [the name of the person] be secure by day, secure by night, and secure at all times, day and night.
One shall attain a lifespan of a hundred years and witness a hundred autumns.
Why is this? Because in the world, there is nothing superior to the Buddha;
he is the Honored One among Heaven and Earth, whom all deities revere and look up to.
If there are those who practice evil spells or incantations—
whether they have already done so, are about to do so,
are doing so in the present, or whether they have succeeded or not— they shall all be extinguished.
Furthermore, regarding all poisons capable of harming people:
wherever this *Ṣaḍakṣarīvidyārājñasūtra* is located,
whether it is read, recited, received, maintained, or remembered there—
All evil karmas and heavy obstacles shall be extinguished.
Then he spoke this mantra:
*khare kharaṭe khavire gaṇau gaṇau tati pāti svāhā*. If anyone should cast an evil spell or curse against such-and-such a person...
Whether already performed or yet to be performed,
by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas,
or any others capable of casting evil spells and curses, may they all be utterly extinguished.
Whether caused by khaṇḍa, vetāla, or pūtana, may all such things be utterly extinguished.
May all evils be completely eliminated and replaced by manifold virtues.
May this mantra be ever auspicious.
By means of these words of truth,
may [Name] be secure by day and secure by night, always secure day and night;
may they attain a lifespan of a hundred years and witness a hundred autumns.
Why is this? Because in the world, there is nothing superior to the Dharma.
It is revered by devas and humans, accepted by all Māras, and is free from desire and attachment.
Then he spoke the mantra:
Khaṭi khaṭu kha-viti | Ghanthu ghanthu | Dhati vati | Svāhā. Why is this? Because there is nothing in the world superior to the Saṅgha.
A field of merit that is virtuous and honored by the noble ones, protected by all who do good.
He then spoke this mantra:
*khaṭi khaṭu kha-viti ghanau ghanau tati vati dauti āneti ācoudi svāhā*. If anyone should cast an evil spell or curse against such-and-such a person...
Whether it be the concoction of poisons, whether genuine or counterfeit, or any unlawful acts committed,
or the various evils performed by one's past or present body—
may all such grave offenses be entirely extinguished.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:

*maheśvara umadevi umādhṛtadevi khaumadevi bhrūmādeve citte cittadevadhṛtadevi abhijñe abhi svāhā*. If there be anyone who can recite and uphold this six-syllable King of Divine Mantras Sūtra, [they shall attain liberation].
If even a withered tree can be made to sprout branches and leaves again by means of a mantra,
how much more so for a human being?
May such-and-such a person attain a lifespan of a hundred years and witness a hundred autumns.
That which was spoken by all Buddhas and transmitted by Ānanda—
if anyone reads and recites it until they have mastered it, they will all be protected by themselves;
all evils will stay far from their person, and they will always be accompanied by goodness.
If one recites this mantra for another, it can eliminate that person’s manifold sufferings, evils, and afflictions.
The reciter must abstain from the five pungent vegetables and maintain a sincere and pure mind before they may practice it.
Thus, all calamities and misfortunes will be eliminated without exception, and nothing will fail to become auspicious.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
*hehe carī hehana mi hehe buddhamati hehe nighaṭa nigruśa hehe nighaṭa khoyuṭa nibiśakhoyuṭa īṇe mīṇe dhāpe dhadhāpe svāhā*. Homage to the Triple Gem.
Homage to the Tathāgata Āryajñānasāgaravairocanavyūharāja.
Homage to all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Homage to the Noble Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
Having thus taken refuge,
he then spoke this divine mantra:
"May this mantra be ever auspicious."
Homage to the Noble Avalokiteśvara. "Behold my body"—
reciting this phrase three times for the sake of his compassion,
he then spoke this mantra:

U-ha-ni-mu-a-ni-a-ta-ni-a-ta-vi-a-ta-ja-vi-ni-dam-vi-ni | An-ta-le | Pa-ta-le | Si-pi-ti | An-ta-ra-ba-si-ni | Sa-lu-du-shre-ta | Pa-ra-du-shre-ta | Chi-dam-yam-ba-ya | Dam-ba-ya-ma-ha-ya-ye-ba-mu-ra | Ti-na-mu-ca-ti | Lu-lu-chi-ta-na-ta-si | Lu-lu-lu-lau-chi-ta-pa-ta-si | Svāhā. This mantra can protect against all calamities and hardships.

Pure and stainless, with the radiant light of liberation, it observes and illuminates all those who bind themselves as thieves and commit evil deeds, so that they no longer wander in delusion; it delivers those who contemplate goodness from all calamities and all malevolent māras.
In this present life, may lions, mad elephants, tigers, wolves, jackals, dogs, monkeys, apes,
and all other predatory beasts that seek to harm me be completely bound.
For the sake of [Name] and his companions traveling with him, I now [make this vow].
May all places where the power of this mantra is directed—whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—be entirely peaceful and auspicious.
Then he spoke the mantra:
*Jihlī jihlī mūlī maṇḍike caṇḍali kṣara kṣara rāye svāhā.* I pay homage to the Triple Gem. May this mantra be most greatly auspicious and effective; employ this mantra-method with skill.
On the day of the ritual, one should bathe to become fresh and clean, removing all impurities.
With body and mind tranquil and composed, one must refrain from sexual intercourse, abstain from the five pungent vegetables, avoid drinking alcohol or eating meat.
If one’s tongue has uttered evil speech, one should take a white thread in hand;
recite the mantra seven times, tying a knot once for each repetition.
Once the cord has been completed, if one is involved in legal affairs or subjected to slander, [one shall be protected].
Should they encounter strife and mutual cursing,

slander, treacherous plots, or any other evils, by means of this incantation, these shall be bound within the person's sash or belt, and all such calamities as described above will be entirely extinguished.
After the ceremony has concluded, invite the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha to burn various sublime incenses.

Prepare a vegetarian feast to invoke blessings, and cultivate profound compassion and reverence to repay the compassionate grace of the Buddhas. The presiding master shall personally untie the knots and make this great vow: "May I and all beings of the four modes of birth forever sever the eight difficulties; may all our aspirations be fulfilled according to our hearts."
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:

*He-dau-ma-ti-ya-she-po-ti, po-lo-sha-tien-po-ti, o-shou-po-ti, yu-to-lo-ni, a-ch'a-ye-po-ti, a-nou-shan-ti-mu-khi-po-lo-po-mu-ti, po-lo-po-chi-dou-svāhā*. Homage to all the Three Jewels—Past, Future, and Present—who eternally abide.
Homage to the Tathāgata, the Holy Ocean of Wisdom, the All-Illuminating Adornment King.
Homage to all the Tathāgatas, the Arhats, the Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Homage to the Holy Avalokiteśvara, the Dispeller of Poisonous Harm, the Savior from Suffering, the Great Compassionate One.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra,
the Bodhisattva Maitreya, the Bodhisattva Apāyajaha,
and the Bodhisattva Śāntendriya.
The Bodhisattva Prajñāśreṣṭha,
the Bodhisattva Nityāvirahita-loka,
and the Śūraṅgama-samādhi-gaganagañja.
The Jewel Banner,
the Peacock King Dhāraṇī,
and the Six-Syllable Verse.
Bhaiṣajyarāja,
Bhaiṣajyasamudgata,
and Dṛḍhamati.
I take refuge in such noble assemblies of those who have attained the Way, including the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas such as Avimalacāritra, each addressed by their respective names.
Thereupon, he spoke this great dhāraṇī mantra.
He then spoke the mantra, saying: Karani-mati.
Viśuddhānigati-bara-vyāsa-śūra-vareḥ
Dhatini dhasandhava tiśadhamukha utarāṇi.
Śataparviviśaviśaṇḍakāriśavasana-bhagati.
Kauśalabāvanī anuṣanti viṣanti jiti.
Ajite tvaṃ nāgade ajatvaṃ nāgade.
Āvāsiri aśasrāṇi brāhmaṇi mūle.
Mura mura pāthale śanivara luḥ sūri-pate jute varalu.
Svimali amali svāhā.
This mantra can eliminate all darkness;
it is upheld by the Tathāgata and reverently received by all devas.
It is that which is protected and remembered by benevolent deities; that which is understood by Brahmā;
that which is reverently served by Śakra and guarded by the World-Protectors;
that which is definitively realized by the various sages and seers; that which is upheld by those of harmonious lineage; and that which liberates one from all fetters.
All devas and humans sever all afflictions, subdue Māra and his enemies,
restrain all heterodox teachers, crush all arrogance, and surpass all Dharma masters in discourse and debate.
There is nothing they do not attain; their roots of goodness increase, their body and mind are purified, and they do not abandon the great assembly.
They find joy in all the dharmas of training, protect the scriptures, and through the profound treasury of Dharma, benefit the Three Jewels.
Out of compassion for all classes of sentient beings,
these dhāraṇī verses of the Treasury of the Inexhaustible— which adorn all meanings and possess such great benefits and advantageous functions—
are capable of providing protection where there is no protection. Furthermore, if there are those who can read, recite, copy, and uphold them, [they shall likewise receive this benefit].
If one causes others to transcribe [this scripture], or even makes offerings of incense and flowers to the scroll,
one shall obtain thirty-two difficulties that are free from doubt and fear.
One who employs this dhāraṇī method should bathe and rinse their mouth at dawn, burn incense, and prostrate with a profound heart.
Having recited this three times and completed these practices, wherever one travels, whatever one speaks,
and in whatever direction the fourfold assembly gazes upon or goes, there shall never fail to be auspiciousness.
The multitude will honor and respect him, and those who see him will rejoice. Enemies will submit;
Ānanda, you all should single-mindedly uphold these verses of this dhāraṇī.

When this Dharma was being preached, all the devas, nāgas, the eight classes of supernatural beings, ghosts, and spirits, having heard what the Buddha taught, were filled with great joy; they prostrated themselves and departed.
*The Sutra of the Six-Syllable Divine Mantra King*.
